fixes.explanation: Wood sounds sturdy, I'll give you that. But the text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Wood never makes the list. These folks made bricks and let them do the job of stone. I once spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I respect anybody who works with what they've got.

A tower falling over before it's done would be a plot twist, but the LORD doesn't say that. He says, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) That's the whole “if” and the whole “then,” right there. I think it's like a group chat where everybody finally agrees on a time. Scary, that kind of teamwork.

I see why you'd pick it, since the tower has been the talk of the whole passage. But the LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) He doesn't say He'll bring the tower down. He goes after their speech, so they can't understand each other.

Not quite, baker. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The scattering came, and the building stopped. I bet that left a pile of bricks and a very confused foreman. Picture trying to say “pass the tar” and getting a blank stare back!
